title: Tenant VPC onboarding: slab playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a pragmatic, repeatable flow for onboarding a customer tenant VPC using a slab-based allocation pattern and complementary Terraform modules. It is intentionally prescriptive for SREs and SEs running the first 1–10 private deployments; later iterations should distill into automation templates and an operator CLI.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Solutions Engineers, Onboarding SREs, Infra PMs, Customer Network Engineers.
- Scope: VPC peering/trunking, subnet slab assignment, route/proxy placement, IP plan validation, TF module parameterization, staged upgrade from staging -> prod.
- Out of scope: application-level ingress policies, customer internal PKI rotation steps (refer to security playbooks).

Terminology (quick):
- Slab: a contiguous CIDR allocation unit we hand to a tenant (e.g., /22) that contains multiple subnets for control plane, inference nodes, and egress.
- Trunking: using a shared transit/edge instance to multiplex tenant traffic to Redwood services.
- Landing zone: minimal set of infra (subnets, NAT, route tables, peering/gateway) we require in customer VPC.

High-level reference architecture (textual diagram):
[Customer VPC]
  - Slab (/22) split -> control-plane-subnet (/26), inference-pool-subnets (/24 x 2), management-subnet (/28)
  - PrivateLink/Transit-GW or Peering -> Redwood edge (Dedicated NAT/egress cluster)
  - Optional: On-prem crossconnect -> direct fiber -> edge appliance -> trunking to Redwood nodes

Prereqs (customer + Redwood):
- Customer provides: desired slab CIDR (RFC1918), allowed egress CIDRs, KMS/FQDN allowlist, contact matrix for network ops, and expected throughput number (Gbps).
- Redwood: prepared TF module versions (see notes), edge egress IP pool, bootstrap inventory for orchestration, and access to customer VPN connection details if applicable.

Terraform module notes (working recommendations):
- Use modules/tenant-vpc-v2 (experimental) not v1 for new onboardings. Major differences: automatic subnet-slicing, explicit route-propagation outputs, and tags for billing.
- Variables we set during onboarding: slab_cidr, env_tag, allowed_egress_list (list of strings), nat_gateway_count (1|2), enable_transit_gw (bool), trunk_bgp_asn (number).
- Required outputs to wire into Redwood control plane: vpc_id, control_plane_subnet_ids (comma separated), inference_subnet_ids, route_table_ids, peering_id_or_tgw_id.
- Keep module state isolated per-tenant in backend with path 'tenants/${tenant_id}/vpc.tfstate' to avoid accidental cross-tenant changes.
- Quick TF snippet (example variables block):
  slab_cidr = "10.64.0.0/22"
  nat_gateway_count = 1
  enable_transit_gw = true

Staged onboarding runbook (recommended sequence):
1) Intake and validation (approx 1–2 business days)
   - Confirm slab is routable within customer environment (no overlap with existing on-prem or other cloud slabs).
   - Validate DNS/KMS/ServiceAccount requirements and legal/dataflow constraints.
   - Get customer signoff on egress IP allowlist.

2) Pre-provisioning (2–4 hours)
   - Create tenant state path in TF backend.
   - Populate variables file with slab and contact info.
   - Dry-run: terraform plan -> capture diff and annotate risky changes.

3) Provision landing zone (30–90 minutes)
   - terraform apply on modules/tenant-vpc-v2 with minimal flags.
   - Verify subnets created in customer account; export outputs.
   - Attach peering or TGW connection; confirm route propagation.

4) Wire control plane (1–3 hours)
   - Use control-plane orchestrator to register control_plane_subnet_ids and set routing policies (hairpin/proxy).
   - Run small canary workload (single inference pod) to validate DNS, MTU, and egress behavior.

5) Scale inference pool and tuning (1–6 hours)
   - Provision inference subnets + autoscaling groups or dedicated nodes.
   - Validate KV cache warmup, large request tail latency, and path MTU with 1500/9001 tests.
   - Enable continuous batching hints in config for the tenant.

6) Observability and rollout (ongoing)
   - Ensure per-token tracing is enabled and routing logs are arriving in Redwood Console (or customer SIEM as configured).
   - Configure healthchecks and canary traffic percentages for first 48 hours.

Upgrade plan: staging -> prod (recommended safe path)
- Motivation: we maintain two TF workspaces per tenant: staging (for validation) and prod (live). The upgrade path mirrors a PR flow: changes are applied to staging, run full validation, then promoted to prod with minimal drift.
Steps:
  a) Branch workflow: all infra changes in GH -> feature branch -> open PR against 'infra/tenants'. Run terraform plan on staging workspace automatically.
  b) Validation gates: network tests (NAT egress ips, MTU, route propagation), security review (allowed ports), traffic shaping test (3-minute burst with synthetic traffic).
  c) Fallback policy: keep last-known-good plan and terraform state snapshot. If prod apply fails, rollback by reapplying last-known-good state and opening incident.

Validation checklist (pre-prod cutover):
- [ ] No CIDR overlap reported by customer network ops.
- [ ] TF plan on staging is non-destructive for control-plane resources.
- [ ] Peering/TGW routes propagate in <= 5 minutes.
- [ ] Egress IPs match allowlist (customer verified).
- [ ] Canary latency/99th-percentile within SLO (compare to hosted baseline).
- [ ] Logs and traces flowing to console and customer SIEM.

Common gotchas and mitigations:
- Overlapping RFC1918 spaces: ask for unique slab; if impossible, use NAT/proxy-only pattern to avoid asymmetric routing.
- Customer uses strict DNS policies: provide split-horizon DNS instructions and FQDN allowlist for health endpoints.
- TGW vs peering limits: TGW recommended when managing >10 tenants to avoid peering scale issues.
- MTU mismatches with on-prem: run iperf and adjust PMTU on edge appliance; report issues to networking team early.

Rollback play (if prod apply causes outage):
1) Immediately revert prod TF to last-known-good state and apply.
2) Force route re-propagation by toggling peering attachments (coordinate with customer).
3) If traffic still failing, shift traffic to Redwood-hosted fallback model (edge routing policy) while we remediate.

Post-onboarding checklist (within 7 days):
- Collect runbook feedback with customer network team.
- Capture any manual fixes as TF module patches and PR back to infra repo.
- Schedule a 30-day review for cost/throughput adjustments.

Operational notes (short tips):
- Tagging standard: tenant:${tenant_id}, env:${env}, owner:${se-team}. Tags must be applied by TF module.
- State security: encrypt TF backend with customer KMS key when required for compliance.
- Monitoring: enable per-tenant SLO dashboards in Redwood Console and configure alerting for 95/99 latency and egress errors.

Appendix A: Example terraform variable file (tenant-vars.tfvars):
slab_cidr = "10.96.0.0/22"
env_tag = "prod"
allowed_egress_list = ["52.23.11.7/32","3.121.8.0/24"]
nat_gateway_count = 2
enable_transit_gw = true
trunk_bgp_asn = 64512

Appendix B: Quick network debug commands (customer VPC side):
- Verify routes: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=${vpc_id}
- Check subnet association: aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=cidr-block,Values=10.96.0.0/22
- Test MTU: ping -M do -s 8972 <redwood-edge-ip>

Appendix C: Postmortem template for onboarding incidents (fill and attach to JIRA-DEPLOY ticket):
- Summary, Timeline, Root cause, Mitigation applied, TF diff, Action items, Owner, ETA.

Notes and TODOs (work in progress):
- Convert slab split logic into reusable module that can produce /26 control-plane and two /24 inference pools automatically. (TODO: PR-487 implements half of this.)
- Validate TGW costs vs peering for high-throughput customers; add cost-estimate generator to onboarding checklist.
- Audit current 20 tenant states for consistent tags and drift.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary: Anjali Mehta (anjali@redwood.ai)
- SE backup: Ethan Cole (ethan@redwood.ai)
- Infra SRE pager: #infra-oncall (Slack)

This doc is a draft and intended to evolve with feedback from field runs. Please annotate the 'issues' section in the linked GH PR or add comments in Confluence page 'private-deployments/tenant-slab-patterns'.
